jobs.occupation: Global Integrity Officer (parental cover)
jobs.description:
Oxfam Denmark is looking for a Global Integrity Office (paternity cover). Main areas of responsibility are:

• Oversee risk, compliance and governance (integrity) frameworks and their execution

• Assurance (internal audit), ad hoc and when time allows

• Coordinate domain owners across EOL and ODK

• Raise risks to appropriate management fora in ODK

A major part of the role relates to https://educationoutloud.org/ - an extensive programme spanning support to civil society organisations in more than 60 countries.

Responsibilities and tasks

Within the period of this parental leave cover from approximately mid-December 2026 to mid-May 2027, the specific tasks are the following and its prioritisation and timing to be agreed with the relevant line manager (EOL Global Programme Manager):

• ODK and EOL’s point of entry for misconduct-cases, triage and coordination with subject-matter-experts (such as for safeguarding, corruption and HR/interpersonal misconduct.

• Periodically present case overview and propose further action to Misconduct Risk Committee.

• Draft case summaries to donors in close coordination with main donor relations staff.

• In connection with the first EOL2 call for proposal, be responsible for:

• Reviewing the current grant management template with an eye to improvements, drawing on past experiences and suggestions for improvement.

• Reviewing the current due diligence process with an eye to improvements, drawing on past experiences and suggestions for improvement.

• Assisting in rolling out the EOL2 Virtual Integrity Team structure, including populating the annual wheel of deliveries and domain owner one-pagers and guiding Regional Management Units (RMUs) in rolling out the same for grantees

• Supporting the integration of findings and data from due diligence, grant monitoring, MEL, audit, financial reporting and integrity-related case management into ongoing risk oversight and decision-making.

• Supporting production and development of monitoring and reporting products for management, governance bodies and GPE, including risk and integrity reporting mechanisms and associated guidance.

• If time and tasks allow, as agreed with the line manager:

• Contribute to finalising the pension procurement

• Contribute to the internal audit of ODK’s main external parties, sourcing history and documentation (contracts, waivers etc.).

Your qualifications and competences

• Academic background and professional seniority and experience relevant to programme and project work will be looked upon favourably.

• NGO-background will be beneficial but is not mandatory.

• The precise composition of tasks will be calibrated to the chosen profile’s skills and experience.

• Strong communication skills in English

We offer

• Preferred start date: 01 December 2026

• Role is a full-time position (37 hours/week including lunch break) but Oxfam Denmark is open to discuss arrangements of fewer hours and their prioritisation. We have flexible working hours including the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days a week.

• Salary and pension according to applicable collective agreement: AC/State.

• The workplace is Oxfam Denmark's office at Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, in the new VOX building together with 11 other NGOs, close to Ryparken Station. Our staff is appx. 70 people.

• We support a lunch scheme in the shared VOX canteen, where the food is predominantly vegetarian.

• Health insurance and massage as gross salary schemes, as well as free weekly yoga.

Application process

Click the Apply button and submit your application and CV to us as soon as possible and no later than 25 October. We will conduct interviews in week 45 and 46.

Please note that we do not accept applications outside of our recruitment system. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply - regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion or age. It is necessary that you are eligible for employment in Denmark.

EOL Global Programme Manager Lars Udsholt (lu@oxfam.dk) can be contacted for further information.

About Oxfam Denmark

Oxfam Denmark is an independent and member-based development organisation. We have the world's best cause and high ambitions. Through education, support to civil society and in collaboration with our partners, we fight inequality and poverty in the Global South. Together with 20+ other organisations, we form the Oxfam International confederation, one of the world's largest and most influential development organisations. In Denmark, we are a clear and significant player in the public debate on issues such as tax havens, rising inequality, climate change and the right to education.

jobs.occupation: 3 Postdoc positions within forest microbiome assisted afforestation
jobs.description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management and Department of Biology, invites applicants for three two-year Postdoc positions within forest microbiome manipulation. The positions are part of the project “MycoForest - Stimulating Forest carbon uptake and storage by mycorrhizal inoculation”, which is financed under the Innomission partnership INNO-CCUS by Innovation Fund Denmark.

Start date is 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

The soil microbiome plays a crucial role in soil- and ecosystem functioning including ecosystem carbon sequestration and support of plant nutrient acquisition.

Denmark is devoted to become carbon neutral by 2045/2050, a goal involving a significant role for biological carbon sequestration and storage. A part of the Danish strategy to reach carbon neutrality is to afforest former agricultural land thereby increasing biological ecosystem carbon capture and storage. However, agricultural soils do not harbor an optimal microbiome for initial tree growth and forest ecosystem development. This may lead to increased mortality, reduced tree growth and slower development of forest soil functions and ultimately non-optimal carbon capture, especially in the early stages of afforestation.

Therefore, the MycoForest project aims to manipulate and assist the microbiome of agricultural soils through mycorrhizal inoculation as an integrated part of tree planting to stimulate tree growth and carbon sequestration. Therefore, MycoForest at University of Copenhagen is hiring three postdocs to become part of this novel journey towards increased biological carbon sequestration and to play key roles in the scientific investigations.

Each of the three postdocs will cover one of three distinct areas of fundamental importance to understand and document the role of the microbiome in afforestation.

The three key areas are:

• Microbial and mycorrhizal fungal development

• Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics

• Tree survival and growth, and carbon uptake

The studies will involve controlled greenhouse as well as field scale experiments, and the three postdocs will each be responsible for one of the three specific parts of the project. At the same time, they will be closely linked to each other through tight collaboration on establishment and sampling of the afforestation experiment. The postdoc positions will start as soon as possible and will run for 2 years. For the requirements of the specific postdocs, please see the descriptions below.

Contact: Specific questions for each of the postdocs, please see below. For general MycoForest questions, please contact Claus Beier, cbe@ign.ku.dk.

Postdoc 1 – Soil microbial development after mycorrhizal inoculation

The post doc will oversee the formulation and addition of fungal or other types of inoculums and will follow and quantify the mycorrhizal fungal colonization of seedlings, root and soil. Experimentation will be both in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions and in the field. Colonization will be followed in different soils and host trees with a combination of classical microscopic techniques and novel molecular methods. The studies aim to document successful establishment of mycorrhizal fungi within the indigenous communities.

Therefore, we are looking for candidates with specific knowledge and hands-on with:

• Fungi in general including mycorrhizal fungi, preferentially ectomycorrhiza

• Field experience in general, handling and sorting soils and roots in specific

• Microscopy, especially stereo microscopy of roots

• DNA extraction og plants and soil and PCR optimizations including qPCR

• Bioinformatics and statistical analysis of meta-barcoding datasets

The post doc will work closely together with PD 2 and 3 for plant and soil responses to inoculations.

Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Rasmus Kjøller, Department of Biology, rasmusk@bio.ku.dk, Phone: +45 35322311

Postdoc 2 – Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics in response to mycorrhizal inoculation

The post doc will study effects of inoculation in different soil types and tree species on soil carbon processes including formation of persistent SOC fractions.  The postdoc will study soil carbon dynamics in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions in close cooperation with postdoc 1 and in field experimental conditions in cooperation with postdoc 3. The project will address how inoculation and changes in the mycorrhizal community composition will affect soil carbon sequestration processes in post-agricultural soils. The studies will shed light on the extent to which inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil will change the soil C input quantity and quality from roots and microbial necromass, eventually enhancing accumulation of persistent forms of SOC.

We are looking for a candidate with a PhD in the fields of soil science and organic matter studies, soil ecology and biogeochemistry. Previous experience with plant-soil interactions in field, mesocosm and laboratory experiments using chemical soil analyses including soil organic carbon (organic matter fractionation and biomarkers targeting microbial and plant origin of organic matter), carbon isotopes, roots, and microbial taxonomic and functional community composition will be considered a plus.

Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Vesterdal, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, lv@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 61670865

Postdoc 3 – Tree responses to mycorrhiza inoculation

The postdoc will establish and follow field experiments in practical afforestation sites and monitor plant responses such as growth and survival, mycorrhizal colonization, and plant community development.

The studies will address the potential of inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil to stimulate survival, growth and carbon draw down of forest trees and communities including the role of tree species and soil type interactions.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a PhD in plant or forestry science and interest and experience in:

• Afforestation, forestry and forest ecology

• Design and analysis of experiments

• Field work and practical application of technology in land management

Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Niclas Scott Bentsen, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, nb@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 20206318.

General qualifications

Apart from the specific qualifications and interests listed above, we look for candidates with general competences in:

• Driver license (mandatory)

• Handling of plants and soil

• Organizing and conducting field sampling

• Data management

• Statistics

• Scientific writing and publishing

Our groups and research – and what do we offer?

The positions are located in three different groups at the university.

Postdoc 1 is with Department of Biology, Fungal Ecology lab within Section of Terrestrial Ecology. The group works with/focuses on mycorrhizal fungal communities and their impact on ecosystem processes and plant health. We apply molecular markers to disentangle these otherwise invisible fungal populations and communities associated with plants and soil. Besides molecular markers, we also apply biochemical markers as well as classic microscopy and microbiological culturing of fungi. Another methodological strongpoint is various mesh-enclosure techniques to study and compartmentalize both the function and community composition of mycorrhizal fungal mycelia in soil.

Postdoc 2 and 3 are with Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, one in the Biogeochemistry group and one in the Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group. In the Biogeochemistry Group we are dedicated to improving the understanding of ecosystem functioning with particular focus on how ecosystems will respond to environmental changes and to management actions. We quantify the pools and fluxes of matter in semi-natural and managed ecosystems and measure the processes related to input and output fluxes in control of soil C stocks to answer questions such as “Can we sequester C in soils by afforestation of cropland soils, and how does this interact with the soil fauna and microbes when using certain tree species or tree species mixtures?” The Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group encompas expertise in forestry, ecological restoration, growth modelling and systems analysis. The group is dedicated to advance the understanding, development, and management of forest ecosystems to support a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon storage, material and energy provision, groundwater regulation, and biodiversity conservation.

Department of Biology is located at Norre Campus and Department of Geosciences on Frederiksberg Campus, close to central Copenhagen. The departments offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environments. The departments are planning to increase their focus on the climate change mitigation potential of forests in upcoming projects. We therefore welcome applications from candidates with a broader interest in the intersection of forests, forest-based climate solutions, biosphere-atmosphere interaction, and related themes.

jobs.description:
The department of Plant and Environmental Sciences invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in faba bean/cereal intercropping. The project is part of the research centre “N2CROP”, which is a centre for legume innovation funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The centre is a partnership between Aarhus University, the Technical University of Denmark, University of Copenhagen, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, and La Trobe University

Start date is (expected to be) 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Intercropping is considered a potential more sustainable cropping system reducing fertilizer and pesticide inputs. Despite the well-known effects of intercropping there is still a knowledge gap considering belowground interactions. The project will focus on intercropping of faba bean and cereals, and the potential benefits of the fun mutant (fixation under nitrate). Above- as well as belowground complementarity and competition between crops will be examined with focus on nitrogen dynamics. The project will also focus on biological nitrogen fixation, transfer of nitrogen between species and effect of specific rhizobium strains on fixation. Experiments will be conducted in field trials and in rhizotubes, and the field experiments will be done in close collaboration with SLU in Uppsala where similar experiments will be carried out. Results from the experiments will feed into development of an intercropping crop modelling part.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of agronomy, biology and/or root science. Applicants can have a background with specific knowledge on root development and function, grain legume production, intercropping, crop competition and biological nitrogen fixation. Experience with greenhouse and/or field studies in combination with one or more of the abovementioned topics is an advantage.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD position is placed in the Belowground Crop Ecology research group headed by Associate professor Dorte Bodin Dresbøll. Focus of the research group is on resilient and sustainable cropping systems with special emphasis on belowground interactions, root development and function. We are working with grain legumes, forage legumes and cereals for food and feed. Main topics of the group are drought tolerance, nutrient acquisition and root exudation.

jobs.description:
The Department of Food Science and the Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in colloidal research in food science. The PhD project has the overall goal of describing the molecular structure of casein micelles through computational and experimental investigations, with focus on the role of κ caseins. The candidate will be part of the CaIFF center for the use of neutrons for the investigation of colloids and interfaces in food science and pharmacy (https://pharmacy.ku.dk/research/caiff/).

Expected start date is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Background. Casein micelles (CMs) are the main protein constituent of milk (80% of protein) and defining for dairy product taste and structure. CMs are 100-200 nm globular particles, formed by a hydrated network of disordered casein proteins, named αS1, αSs, β, and κ casein. The caseins are cross-linked through binding to ionic calcium and colloidal calcium phosphate, and through hydrophobic interactions. Post-translational modifications play an important role in this, as the ionic interactions are largely mediated by casein phosphorylation sites. The CMs are stabilized by κ caseins that are believed to form a hairy layer on the CM surface. Therefore, κ casein are particularly important for CM stability. κ caseins moreover contain a rennet cleavage site, separating its anchoring para κ casein domain from the water-soluble caseinomacropeptide, the primary component of the stabilizing hairy layer. Enzymatic cleavage of this site promotes coagulation and curd formation.

Goal. Despite decades of research, central questions remain regarding the CM structure, their molecular organization, and dynamic behaviour. The goal of the PhD project is to answer fundamental questions like: are all caseins needed for CM formation? What is the role of post-translational modifications in the casein-calcium network formation, and in the κ casein hairy layer? How extended is the stabilizing hairy layer, and how does it depend on for example pH or solvent? What is the dynamic exchange of caseins between soluble caseins or other CMs? In other words, the PhD project’s aim is to understand the molecular interactions in CM which are central to the unique food properties of dairy products like milk, cream, and cheese, with a particular focus of κ casein.

How. Methodological strategy involves state-of-the-art molecular dynamics simulations for building a molecular model of casein micelles. Advanced x-ray and neutron scattering experiments, will be used to validate the model. Scattering experiments provide information of the hierarchical structure of CMs, whereas molecular simulations model the molecules and their interactions. The combination of simulations and scattering data is particularly strong, as the simulated molecular predictions can be validated experimentally. The project thus involves preparing samples, collecting and analysing scattering data and complementary data when needed, and running MD simulations and comparing these to the experimental data. [AL1]

Societal impact. By understanding casein micelles better, the project supports the development of more sustainable dairy products based on plant-based or precision fermented proteins. Such approaches could remedy the green house gas emissions and adverse effect on biodiversity and animal welfare in traditional dairy production.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for applicants with a strong background in molecular modelling, for example applied to food or structural biology. Experience with any of the following is an advantages:

• Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations; coarse-grained force fields, for example Martini.

• Small-angle x-ray scattering (SAXS), small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) or other x-ray or neutron scattering experiments.

• Programming, for example use of Python and GitHub.

• Data analysis, inverse problems and statistical analysis.

• Mathematical understanding, knowledge of integration, Fourier transformation etc.

• Wet lab experience; protein purification, experience with with colloidal and self-assembled systems.

Finally, the candidate needs to posses good written and oral communication skills.

Our group and research – and what we offer?

You will be part of a very strong cross-institutional and international research environment through the CaIFF center (https://pharmacy.ku.dk/research/caiff/). This means that other PhD students will start approximately at the same time, and you will be part of a unique network of young researchers in the center. You will be supervised by newly appointed tenure track assistant professor Andreas Larsen as well as associate professor Jacob Kirkensgaard (https://www.erda.dk/vgrid/JJKK/), who are affiliated with the Department of Food science and the Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen. Thus, you will be in a research environment focusing on self-assembly, dynamic structure formation within food science, but also have colleques in the related field of polymer science and soft matter. You will get regular supervision and be part of a lively research group with students at all level from BSc to PhDs and postdocs. A strong methodological focus core technique in the group is on the use of x-ray and neutron scattering experiments to probe structure and molecular self-assembly at the nanometer-scale.

The Departments offers unique facilities. Department of Food science have state-of-the art laboratory facilities for sample preparation and characterization. Computational resources are available through national and European supercomputer facilities LUMI and Computerome, along with local small-scale GPU resources at the Niels Bohr Institute. Local SAXS instrument are available at both institutes, and managed through the cross-disciplinary X-ray center (CXC), and thereby readily available for the project. Only one hour from the University of Copenhangen, in Lund in Sweden, there is access to the world-class x-ray synchrotron MAX-IV, and the project involves SAXS experiments there. Moreover, the group regularly visits neutron facilities in Europe, and will be frequent users of the neutron facility European Spallation Source (ESS) also in Lund, which is expected to open for users during 2027.
